instruction.text: Drag the parts of the story into the correct time order.

atoms.text: Gerard the giraffe had a short neck. He struggled to eat leaves at the very top of the trees. One day, he set out to find new ways to reach them.
He tried standing on wooden boxes at first. The boxes were just a little too short, and he still could not reach the top. He would have to try something else.
Then, he tried to find a long pole. Gerard put the pole in his mouth and tried to shake the leaves until they came down. This did not work very well, and his mouth was very sore.

instruction.text: Drag the parts of the story into the correct time order.

atoms.text: Gerard thought about it some more and ignored how sore his mouth was. Maybe he could try wearing sticky gloves and climb the tree! Oh wait, he has hooves. What to do?
After thinking even longer and harder, Gerard talked with some of his friends about his problem. They all thought for a long time too. They had all sorts of ideas!

His friends suggested stacking rocks, pulling branches lower and asking the birds for help, but none of their suggestions sounded good to Gerard, who was feeling sadder and sadder with every failed idea.

instruction.text: Drag the parts of the story into the correct time order.

atoms.text: “I know!” said Gerard’s long-necked friend Fiona, “I can pick the leaves for you and then we can share!”
“But then, how can I help you?” asked Gerard, who wanted to be able to help Fiona in return.
“Why Gerard, you can do what you do best! You can help me when we go to the river to find all the best spots!”
